item: GET /api/sources reads the eight columns it serves and builds no Source entity (audit 0.5.0 A-025, v0.5.1 item 30)
refs: PR #1522; coordinator ruling 26 Oct 23:42; audit A-025; RELEASE_0.5_GATE.md section 1d item 30
summary: list_sources selected full Source entities (24 columns) and read eight attributes off each. It now selects the eight columns (id, name, domain, rss_url, rate_limit_ms, enabled, priority, tags) and maps them to the same dict: same 17,080,350-byte body at 86,000 sources. Measured on 86,000 synthetic sources through the route (real source text is longer, so read the ratio): median over 5 GETs on the OSM lane's box, full list 3,370 ms to 1,299 ms and fields=id,name,rss_url 2,743 ms to 973 ms; RC2's independent re-run on its own box (nothing else running), full list 3,511 ms to 1,492 ms (rerun 1,522) and fields 3,000 ms to 1,113 ms, so about 2.3-2.6x and 2.7-2.8x; bodies byte-identical. The memory figure (184 MB to 46 MB, query alone, tracemalloc on) is one run on one box and is inferred, not re-measured. The rest is JSON serialisation of the rows, not touched (no cap, no new field). tests/test_sources_list_columns.py pins the response row for row against the entity read it replaces (stand-in source left out, limit/offset/fields unchanged) and the SELECT shape: one SELECT on sources naming exactly the eight columns, and no Source entity load (an event listener on Source 'load'); putting the entity query back fails that test. Needs an independent re-measure (RC2) before merge.
